record.original_question: For the tetrahedral graph cocycle action on the space of Nambu-Poisson brackets, determine whether the action is nontrivial or instead trivial in the sense of being generated only by a coordinate change.

evidence.quote: Using the Kontsevich-Nambu micro-graphs in dimensions d >= 2, we explore the open problem of (non)triviality for Kontsevich's tetrahedral graph cocycle action on the space of Nambu-Poisson brackets.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Let $d\ge 2$ and consider $\mathbb{R}^d$ with coordinates $x^1,\dots,x^d$. A Nambu–Poisson bracket on $\mathbb{R}^d$ is a Poisson bivector $P^{ij}$ of the form
$$P^{ij}(x)=\varrho(x)\,\frac{\partial(x^i,x^j,a_1,\dots,a_{d-2})}{\partial(x^1,\dots,x^d)},$$
where $\varrho\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)$ is a density and $a_1,\dots,a_{d-2}\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d)$ are Casimir functions, and the right-hand side is the Jacobian determinant. Kontsevich's graph complex associates to every suitable graph cocycle $\gamma$ (a linear combination of oriented graphs satisfying the cocycle condition $\mathrm{d}\gamma=0$) a universal infinitesimal deformation $\dot P=\mathcal{O}r(\gamma)(P)$ that preserves the Jacobi identity, i.e. defines a class in Poisson cohomology. The simplest nontrivial such cocycle is the tetrahedron $\gamma_3$ on four vertices and six edges.

The deformation $\dot P=\mathcal{O}r(\gamma_3)(P)$ is called trivial on a class of Poisson structures if, restricted to that class, it is a coboundary in Poisson cohomology, i.e. there exists a vector field $X$ (depending on $P$) with $\dot P=[\![P,X]\!]$ (the Schouten bracket), so that $\dot P$ is generated by an infinitesimal change of coordinates.

It is known that on the class of Nambu–Poisson brackets the tetrahedral flow is trivial in this sense for $d=2$, $d=3$, and $d=4$.

Problem. Determine whether Kontsevich's tetrahedral graph cocycle action on the space of Nambu–Poisson brackets on $\mathbb{R}^d$ is nontrivial for some $d\ge 5$, or whether for every $d\ge 2$ this action is trivial in the sense that the induced flow $\dot P=\mathcal{O}r(\gamma_3)(P)$ is, on every Nambu–Poisson bracket $P$, a coboundary $[\![P,X]\!]$ for some vector field $X$ (i.e. generated by a coordinate change).
artifact.category_tag: Kontsevich graph cocycles and Poisson geometry
artifact.status_search_result: The tetrahedral cocycle action on Nambu–Poisson brackets is known to be trivial (a coboundary, induced by a coordinate change) in dimensions d=2 (Kontsevich, 1996), d=3 (Buring–Kiselev–Rutten, 2020), and d=4 (recent work, 2024). The general (non)triviality question for d≥5, and whether any nontrivial graph-cocycle action exists on Nambu–Poisson brackets at all, remains open.
